environment: Disposable Hardhat chain and MySQL database; no Pi deployment
checks: Independent registration stores and displays an arbitrary business type; the business participates in the same dynamic custody flow.
Four independent businesses signed up, registered on chain and signed in without invitations.
Dynamic field labels/values round-trip through stored JSON, operator details and the on-chain metadata hash; invalid or duplicate fields are rejected before storage.
Scanning does not transfer; explicit receipt changes holder without membership. Retries are idempotent; stale/conflicting claims are rejected.
Generic production simulation makes no changes; registered singles require quantity-aware removal rather than generic close.
One business receives products from two independent producers; inventory spans workspaces while unrelated private metadata stays hidden.
All seven generic mutation simulations reject closed products; retired proposal/accept/cancel routes are absent.
Distributor closes its current product without Shop role or production membership; non-holder close and receiving a closed product fail.
Public tracking keeps named holders, product details, dates and short IDs. Private products stay hidden, and sync respects explicit unpublishing.

Registration validates required IDs/counts before storage; duplicate business IDs remain separate records, with confirmed unique aliases including private registrations and exact paginated public search.

Partial receipts conserve global quantity, aggregate stock across six independent paths and three holders, preserve return lineage, paginate without changing totals, and reject stale/oversized/self receipts.
One 100,000-item removal produces one event; owner-only removals preserve written on-chain reasons and category totals, and the batch closes only after all routes reach zero.
Simultaneous receivers of the same source version cannot overdraw stock: exactly one transaction confirms.
Projection is repeatable and rebuildable, rejects inconsistent quantity events atomically, and quantity queries are isolated by contract deployment.
Business-code reservations support custom values, reject conflicts, reuse existing reservations, roll back safely and grow from one character to two, then three.
Concurrent transactions allocate different automatic business codes and serialize retries for the same business.
Custom-code signup rejects an occupied code without leaving an account or key file; a free custom code registers successfully.
Actual migration runners and legacy temporary-table dashboard/public-history integration checks pass on the upgraded schema.
Projector runs repeatedly without duplicate custody receipts; confirmed journals remove serialized transactions.
An interrupted prepared write blocks a new transaction for the same business until the original operation is recovered.
Disabling broadcasts blocks both generic and operator writes without creating journal entries or changing chain state.
additionalChecks: Existing-business automatic migration backfill assigns missing codes, preserves custom codes and remains idempotent across repeated migration/CLI runs.
